fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Archetypes as Tools of Mass Persuasion", "body": "Wayne McRoy Jr. opens with the premise of The Demic of Pan: that archetypes and mythology are used to steer public consciousness while most people remain unaware of it. He points to The Changing Images of Man, a Stanford institute project he says drew on Margaret Mead and, he believes, Joseph Campbell, as an admission that subjective ideas like archetype and allegory can reshape public behavior. In his view the aim is to install a new god called science, woven into news narratives that act on the unconscious before surfacing as behavior, and he argues the pandemic response was planned long in advance."}, {"title": "Transhumanism and the Mind Uploading Promise", "body": "Wayne describes a push toward what he calls hyper materialism, a mindset that treats the five senses as all there is. If consciousness is only an electrochemical byproduct of the brain, the argument runs, it can be copied by an algorithm and uploaded to a machine. He asks who would sit outside that machine running it, calling the upload an abdication of free will and an antichrist spirit in the sense of an alternate Christ. He links the project to Nietzsche's Ubermensch and self-guided evolution, and argues entropy dooms any such control grid, while Chance adds that inharmonic technology lacks nature's self-ordering centropy."}, {"title": "Jehovah, Natural Law and the Inversion", "body": "Chance offers his etymological reading of Jehovah as a verb for self-existing life force, or simply existence, and sets scientism, faith in man's idea of how things work, against following natural law. On that reading, he says, antichrist means salvation through non-existence, which is what he sees the metaverse offering, and the transhumanist promise mirrors the New Age claim that we are literally god. Joshua Donohew adds that placing the letter shin in the middle of YHWH yields Yahshua, salvation, and contrasts the tree of life with a tree of knowledge whose fruit brings death, describing the body itself as a temple."}, {"title": "Numbers, Gematria and Cybernetic Control", "body": "Wayne argues that the controllers try to quantify everything, the divine included. He notes that the letters of the tetragrammaton, YHWH, carry the values 10, 5, 6 and 5, adding to 26, and ties that total to the 26 letters of English, which he calls a carefully crafted language that hides older meanings. Chance suggests a hidden priest class used gematria to keep symbolic meanings consistent across scattered languages. Wayne then defines cybernetics as the science of whole systems control, calling it an inversion of ancient alchemical principles, applied to bodies, minds and economies through feedback loops that find the input for a desired output."}, {"title": "Consent, Symbolic Literacy and Spiritual Armor", "body": "Asked for solutions, Wayne says the answer is to remove consent and reject every offer, mandates included, because he holds that the controllers' power is only perceived. He reads entertainment as entering and taking hold of the mind, and calls bread and circuses the comfort that keeps people compliant. Chance counters that nature, lived in alignment, already offers the abundance and beauty those circuses imitate, and symbolic literacy is offered as a form of psychic self-defense. Joshua Donohew frames the struggle through Ephesians 6, saying that studying these archetypes rather than dismissing them is how one puts on the armor of God against the Hellenism hack."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Wayne McRoy Jr. returns to InnerVerse to discuss his newest book, The Demic Of Pan: Breaking The Natural Order. Supporting as co-host in this chat is Joshua Donohew, as we overview the ritual magic and archetypal influences on the psyche of the masses, the "hellenism hack" and the inverse alchemy of transhumanism, and much more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we explore Wayne's hypothesis that controllers plan to skip the Age of Aquarius, modern medical practices as occult ceremony, cognates to Pan such as Hermes and Enki, the Ahrimanic influence, internet as "mirror world" and the alien invasion within our psyche.
